---
title: "Package release"
description: "Versions the package, tags it and drafts a GitHub release with semantic-release."
---

`package-release.yml` runs [semantic-release](https://semantic-release.gitbook.io)
on `main`. From the [Conventional Commits](commitlint.qmd) since the last
release it

1. works out the next version (`fix:` → patch, `feat:` → minor,
   breaking change → major) — no release if nothing qualifies;
2. writes it to `DESCRIPTION` and commits that as
   `chore(release): set Description file to <version>`;
3. tags the commit with the plain version (`1.2.0`, no `v` prefix);
4. drafts a GitHub release with generated release notes — publish it
   yourself after a final look.

It is normally started by the [release chain](release.qmd), not directly.

## Configuration

If your repository has a `.releaserc.json` in its root, it is used as is.
Otherwise the shared configuration of this repository is used, read at the
ref given by `config-ref`.

Only `desc` is installed for R. If your own configuration runs R code that
needs more packages, the release will fail on the missing package.

## Dry run

With `dry-run: true`, semantic-release checks its access, works out the
next version and prints the release notes — but prepares, commits, tags and
publishes nothing. Useful for testing the chain on a real repository.
